content:
Got old pills sitting in the medicine cabinet? Tomorrow is your chance to get rid of them safely — and keep them out of the wrong hands.

The Drug Enforcement Administration is holding its National Take Back Day on Saturday, October 24, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., and Laredo has five drop-off sites where residents can turn in old or unused medication for safe disposal, according to KGNS.

The Laredo drop-off locations are: KGNS, the Laredo Fire Department at 616 East Del Mar Boulevard, Laredo College South Campus, Texas A&M International University (TAMIU), and the City of Laredo Health Department. Residents with questions can call (956) 754-0912.

Why it matters: unused prescription drugs are one of the most common sources of misuse — they get taken from medicine cabinets, shared with friends or family, or flushed where they can reach the water supply. Take Back Day exists to break that chain. The DEA runs the program nationally, and local sites make it as easy as a Saturday-morning errand.

No appointment, no questions, no cost — just bring the bottles and hand them over. It is a small act of community safety that takes ten minutes.

Sources: KGNS, "DEA Take Back Day offers drug disposal sites in Laredo" (October 23, 2026) — https://www.kgns.tv/2026/10/23/dea-take-back-day-offers-drug-disposal-sites-laredo/

title: Clean Out the Medicine Cabinet: DEA Take Back Day Hits Laredo Saturday
